_note: Industry, peers, street, ownership, moat, critiques, gaps for Tech Mahindra. Every item dated on or before 30-Sep-2026 with its URL. Broker rows from notes/press roundups 29-Jun to 28-Sep-2026; null = not disclosed.

industry.fact: US H-1B fee of USD 100,000 on new applications (proclamation 19-Sep-2025); BSE IT index -2.7% on 22-Sep-2025.
Anthropic's Claude Cowork plug-ins (30-Jan to 3-Feb-2026): Nifty IT -5.87% on 4-Feb-2026, its worst day since March 2020.
Anthropic post on modernising COBOL with Claude Code and Citrini Research's 'contract cancellation' note: Nifty IT -5.3% intraday to 29,875 on 24-Feb-2026.
Jan-Feb 2026 falls: TCS -19%, Infosys -20%, HCLTech -16%, Wipro -23.5%, Tech Mahindra -12% (smallest of the ten Nifty IT stocks); February was the index's worst month since Sep-2008.
Nifty IT -31% in H1 CY2026, on course for its worst year since 2008; Tech Mahindra's 52-week low was Rs1,304.25 on 9-Mar-2026.
Market value of TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech and Tech Mahindra fell to Rs18.15 lakh cr in Jul-2026 from Rs33.71 lakh cr in Aug-2024 (-46%).
Nifty IT -11.2% in Sep-2026 and closed at 27,704.80 on 30-Sep-2026 (about -28% in 2026 against Nifty 50 -13.4% at 22,620.45; Iran war, Brent ~USD103, FPI selling).
HCLTech CEO: 'Something that was a $100 million deal may now be an $80 million'; expects AI to deplete legacy revenue 2-3% a year while AI services grow 30-45%. FY27 guidance 1-4% CC.
Accenture (Q3 FY26): revenue +3% LC, bookings -3%; CEO: client tech budgets 'haven't been increasing' even with AI ('they're spending it differently').
TCS Q1 FY27 revenue roughly flat QoQ; headcount 593,798, down ~19,000 YoY; discretionary projects subdued, budgets moving from conventional application work to AI.
Infosys cut FY27 CC growth guidance to 1.5-3.0% (from 1.5-3.5%) citing softer volumes and pricing.
Cognizant cut 2026 guidance to 4.0-5.5% CC; CEO on large deals: 'you could pass on that productivity to clients'.
Gartner (Jul-2026): 2026 IT spending +14.2% to USD 6.37 tn, but IT services only +5.3%, down from the 8.7% it forecast in Oct-2025.
EPAM cut 2026 organic CC growth guidance to 2-3%; Americas +0.5%.
NASSCOM: FY26 industry revenue USD 315 bn (+6.1%), AI revenue USD 10-12 bn, similar growth expected in FY27; 'AI is compressing traditional work but expanding other areas'.
TCS Q1 FY27 TCV USD 9.5 bn incl. an USD 800 mn AI-led deal; annualised AI revenue USD 2.6 bn (+13.6% QoQ).
Infosys: AI work 8.2% of revenue; Q1 FY27 large-deal TCV USD 3.6 bn (61% net new).
Accenture: 'AI will be a tailwind for us and our industry as it scales'; Middle East conflict cost ~USD 100 mn of quarterly revenue.
HCLTech kept FY27 guidance at Q1 with record net new bookings of USD 2.4 bn, but Q1 EBIT 16.9% was below its band.
Wipro Q1 FY27 IT services revenue -1.2% QoQ CC; Q2 guide -1.5% to +0.5%.
JP Morgan cut Indian IT target P/Es by 25% and large-cap medium-term growth to ~3%; later said the sector is 'only two years into' GenAI deflation and models scale firms at 12-15x.
ICICI Securities reset large-cap target multiples to long-term average minus 2 standard deviations (TCS TP Rs1,860, Infosys Rs950); TCV-revenue gap signals AI deflation in the existing book.

Kotak: incumbent IT worth between 11-12x (no terminal growth) and 17-18x (needs sustained 4-5% CC growth); assumes AI deflation of ~3-3.5% a year to FY29, clients keep ~half of savings; new demand cycle only around CY2027-28.
Jefferies: application managed services (22-45% of revenue) face sharp AI deflation; worst case -3pp revenue CAGR over FY26-31 and a further 30-65% de-rating.
JM Financial: NSE IT index at ~16x one-year-forward consensus EPS, fourth year of subdued growth; Tech Mahindra Add, TP Rs1,705, preferred over Wipro on large-deal ramp-ups.
Rupee closed at 95.81-95.83/USD on 30-Sep-2026 (-1.2% in Jul-Sep).
Forecasts: BMI 97 by Mar-2027 and 99 by Mar-2028 (18-Aug); Axis Bank 97 by Dec-2026, 100 by Jun-2027 (17-Sep).

points: Telecom domain depth (OSS/BSS, networks, Comviva software) is real but concentrated in a slow-growing, cost-cutting client base
No scale advantage versus TCS/Infosys/HCLTech; margins ~10 points below TCS
Switching costs in run/managed-services contracts, but these are the contracts AI productivity pass-backs hit first
Mahindra group parentage helps (group IT work, brand) but is not a moat

critiques: Margin expansion has come from cost (subcontractor cuts, SG&A consolidation, FX) more than pricing; after 15% the easy levers are used and management has not set a path beyond FY27.

FY27 growth is flattered by a European auto programme delivered early (Q2 headwind 1-1.3%) and by large-deal ramp-ups that peers also report; book-to-bill (LTM TCV USD 4.1 bn on USD 6.5 bn revenue) is not exceptional.
Communications is 32% of revenue with 'clearly volatility in a large US telecoms client'.
Reported PAT has been hit by FX hedge losses (Rs480 cr in FY26) while the rupee fall boosts EBIT; the two partly offset.
At ~18x FY28E EPS the stock trades at a ~35% premium to Tier-1 peers that have de-rated by about 40% (HDFC Securities, Jefferies, BOB note the premium).
